critical_code_review_comments: contract.ts (transport): TRANSPORT_VERSION='semantic-1.2', PREVIOUS_TRANSPORT_VERSIONS=['semantic-1.1']; TurnResponse.sessionId/requestId are now 'string | null' and correlationId is optional/nullable with the comment stating it is required on not_accepted errors and absent on success; ErrorCode union adds 'internal_error_unaccepted'. Verified empirically: errors carry UUID correlationId, successes do not.

response-validation.ts (buildVariants per version): 1.2 adds consistency rules success_without_identity, correlation_on_success, missing_correlation, accepted_without_identity — every outgoing body in the independent run and the full L1/L2 suites passes validateTransportResponse.

popResolvedInfeasible: when the top question is an infeasible clarification still open after U1 and an applied op resolves it (per criterion→slot map), the question is popped (openQuestionCount back to the predecessor). Verified across D03-a (answer drop:dates) and D03-b (end_time 18:00 textual).

rca of the issue: No defect found. All seven D-U2C-02 invariants verified in the independent run: (1) invalid/non-canonical ids → null in not_accepted body with correlationId UUID; (2) valid ids preserved separately; (3) 1.1 requests → 400 unsupported_contract (no automatic compatibility); (4) capabilities exposes supportedVersions=['semantic-1.2'] and previousVersions=['semantic-1.1']; (5) success bodies carry NO correlationId; (6) ack_lost → outcome_unknown with original ids and nextAction=get_request, with get_request returning pending and the same requestId reclaimable via takeover after expireLease; (7) throw_before → outcome_unknown (NOT internal_error_unaccepted), get_request → not_found, retry → new attempt. All five D-U2C-03 invariants verified: (a) criterion-scoped invalid_value question with the correct options list; (b) non-pertinent follow-up keeps the same question id and does NOT re-invoke the planner; (c) answering with the correct drop:* resolves exactly one planner call and one revision; (d) 'other' is resolvable by any reformulation, dismiss_question or reset; (e) criteria are byte-identical before/after an infeasible turn except for the user ops themselves.
